source_review.notes: Checked current NIST Technical Note 1297 overview, reporting, and uncertainty-propagation pages; official NASA Risk Management Handbook v2 Parts 1 and 2, RIDM Handbook, Decision Analysis guidance, and NASA-HDBK-7009A; official GAO representation for GAO-20-195G; and NASA Cost Estimating Handbook Appendix J. NIST, NASA web/standards, three of four NTRS retrieval attempts, and Appendix J returned HTTP 200. One NTRS Part 2 attempt timed out and GAO returned HTTP 403 to the command-line client after their current official representations had been inspected through the web retrieval path. The chapter keeps measurement uncertainty, statistical coverage, posterior credibility, prediction, population tolerance, simulated forecast probability, model credibility, and deliberative decision confidence semantically distinct.

evidence: Reviewed gradient-covariance propagation, Wilson interval, Bayes relation, zero-failure bound, complete uncertainty-assertion tuple, independent-component special case, predictive integral, and conditional joint confidence.

Confirmed sample success count, sample size, normal quantile, standard/combined/expanded uncertainty, sensitivity coefficients, covariance, coverage factor, parameter, data, model, and threshold symbols are introduced before use.
Confirmed interval sidedness and parameter-versus-future-outcome semantics remain explicit.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes measurements, sampling parameters, future outcomes, population coverage, forecast events, model evidence, and decisions.

evidence: Executed binomial-confidence-check and reproduced estimate 0.8000; Wald interval 0.7216 to 0.8784; Wilson interval 0.7112 to 0.8666; zero-failure n=100 lower bound 0.9705; and one-of-one Wald 1.0000 to 1.0000 versus Wilson 0.2065 to 1.0000.
Independently recomputed Exercise 1 Wald interval 0.8168 to 0.9832 and corrected the Wilson center/half-width to 0.87146/0.08506, giving 0.7864 to 0.9565 before completion.
Recomputed Exercise 2 combined uncertainty sqrt(17)=4.123 and independence case sqrt(13)=3.606.
Recomputed zero-failure bounds 0.05^(1/100)=0.97048695 and 0.05^(1/200)=0.98513296, and required count ceiling ln(0.05)/ln(0.99)=299.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All displayed arithmetic now agrees with independent recomputation; the review identified and corrected one Wilson half-width/interval error before completion.

evidence: Confirmed the covariance propagation equation is the quadratic gradient form and reduces to squared sensitivity-weighted components under independence.
Derived the one-sided zero-failure bound from the probability of observing no failures R^n=alpha at the lower confidence boundary.
Confirmed solving alpha^(1/n)>=R_target requires n>=ln(alpha)/ln(R_target) because both logarithms are negative.
Confirmed the Bayesian predictive expression integrates conditional outcome variability over posterior parameter uncertainty.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: All relations are explicitly conditional on model, population, sampling, independence/dependence, and applicability assumptions.

evidence: Challenged binomial boundary data, zero failures, small samples, one- versus two-sided intervals, optional stopping, selection, multiplicity, nonrepresentative trials, dependence, common causes, censoring, and configuration drift.

Reviewed measurement bias/resolution/calibration, covariance, nonlinear propagation, Type A/Type B mislabeling, specification-versus-uncertainty confusion, coverage-factor assumptions, and heterogeneous populations.

Reviewed model form, calibration/validation reuse, extrapolation, discarded solver failures, Monte Carlo sampling error versus physical uncertainty, narrow but biased intervals, structural ensembles, expert disagreement, tails, and marginal/joint confidence.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for exact semantics, evidence, assumptions, affected populations, adverse cases, decision authority, and residual ignorance.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: High-stakes applications still require relevant domain, statistical/metrology, modeling, safety, security, privacy, human-factors, economic, ethics, regulatory, operational, and affected-stakeholder review.

evidence: Traced claim/baseline/population identity, uncertainty inventory, contextual reducibility, interval semantics, measurement budget, dependence, representativeness, sparse-evidence limits, non-substitution of confidence types, calibration/model discrepancy, evidence quality, and decision reporting throughout the module.
Confirmed every numerical confidence statement retains a named model, evidence source, population/scenario, configuration, and limitations.
Confirmed simulations are treated as conditional model exploration rather than empirical evidence and new operational drift reopens claims under change control.
Confirmed residual ignorance drives resilience, margin, monitoring, staged decisions, and safe states rather than invented probability.
invariant_checking.notes: No interval or probability is reused across incompatible claims, baselines, populations, or semantic frameworks.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents established estimation and propagation relations but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed confident, reliable, safe, accurate, precise, calibrated, validated, representative, independent, robust, current, demonstrated, and complete language for exact evidence scope.
artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-045/report.json records exact local execution evidence for the declared binomial calculations only.

Measurement, test, historical, operational, supplier, expert, simulation, calibration, validation, and stakeholder evidence remains qualified by configuration, sampling, provenance, dependence, model, population transfer, uncertainty, and limits.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review is claimed. A narrow interval, favorable fraction, high confidence level, many simulations, or independent review is never presented as proof of system correctness, safety, or future performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked uncertainty, aleatory/epistemic context, measurand, measurement/standard/combined/expanded uncertainty, confidence/credible/prediction/tolerance intervals, cost/schedule confidence, calibration, sharpness, model form, and decision confidence. Error, tolerance, variability, ignorance, coverage, posterior probability, prediction, and acceptance remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked Wilson/Wald boundary behavior, measurement covariance, parameter versus prediction, zero failures, model disagreement, joint confidence, selection bias, expert disagreement, drift reopening, flawed Monte Carlo claims, and an autonomous ferry. Each ties uncertainty semantics to evidence, applicability, action, authority, and residual risk.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from claim and inventory through measurement budgets, frequentist/Bayesian/predictive/tolerance semantics, model form/validation/calibration, joint and sparse evidence, multiplicity/expert/update practices, information versus mitigation, decision confidence, communication, and residual ignorance. Ten examples and five complete answers require interval, propagation, bound, adversarial-audit, and sociotechnical case reasoning.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, statistics, metrology, uncertainty-quantification, modeling, systems, decision-science, cost, schedule, architecture, mechanical, electrical, thermal, software, data, control, autonomy, maritime, reliability, safety, security, privacy, accessibility, human-factors, economics, ethics, supplier, operations, verification, validation, regulatory, clinical, passenger, community, or affected-stakeholder review is claimed.
